headline: NQ futures hold 29,422.75, down 0.09%, mid-band after rejecting the 29,364.00 overnight low, while Brent above $101 and a 4.84% 10-year keep Stress extreme into the 12:30 UTC PPI block
body:
The Nasdaq-100 closed the 9 September session at 29,421.55, down 0.29%, inside a 29,334.40-29,563.60 range of about 0.78% and roughly 38% up from the session low. That was a third consecutive decline for the major US indices, with the S&P 500 down 0.48% and the Nasdaq Composite down 0.64%. In the current overnight hour NQ futures trade at 29,422.75, down 0.09%, essentially level with the cash close and mid-way through a 29,364.00-29,480.25 band of about 0.40%. Price probed the overnight low earlier in the session and was rejected; the recovery back to mid-band is the single most important observation for Tail, because meaningful retracement is exactly what the pathological price path denies. Asian cash is weaker, with MSCI's Asia-Pacific ex-Japan index, the Nikkei and the KOSPI all down about 1%, but that weakness has not transmitted into index futures.

The macro regime is genuinely stressed and explains the 81% Stress reading. Brent traded to $101.4 early Thursday after breaking $100 on Wednesday, with WTI near $96.02; crude is up roughly 15% over the month and about 54% over the year on the US-Iran tanker conflict and disrupted transits through the Strait of Hormuz, now compounded by escalation between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis. The 10-year Treasury yield is 4.8406% after reaching 4.857% on Wednesday, its highest since November 2023, with the 2-year at 4.39% and the 30-year at 5.25%; Treasury also said it would triple long-dated buyback operations to $6 billion. Futures price roughly 60% odds of a rate hike at the 15-16 September FOMC. Against that, the VIX is only 16.46, up 4.71%, an absolute level consistent with a functioning mean-reversion environment rather than a disorderly one.

Index internals are dispersed rather than aligned, which further argues against one-way structure. Meta closed up 6.55% at 653.69 on the launch of its Muse consumer AI agent, while the broader megacap complex was mostly lower and Nvidia fell 0.91% on a report that the Justice Department is examining whether its $20 billion Groq licensing deal was structured to avoid antitrust premerger review. Semiconductors were mixed, with AMD, Micron, Qualcomm and Intel higher against Nvidia and Broadcom lower. Shared cross-asset context collected at 00:40 UTC is now beyond its 90-minute freshness limit and was therefore treated as stale supporting material only, with no weight in the price-path assessment.

Confidence is 88%. Current index and futures levels, ranges, the VIX, the 2-year, 10-year and 30-year yields, WTI and Brent, the Asian session path and the seven-day calendar were all verified directly, with FOMC dates taken from the Federal Reserve calendar and the delayed EIA release time confirmed against the holiday schedule. The residual uncertainty is the outcome of releases that have not printed.

lookbackSummary: Twenty-three of the preceding 24 clock-hours carry a published Claude assessment; the 10:00-11:00 UTC slot on 9 September has none and is marked unavailable. Tail ran between 7% and 9% through the Asian and European overnight, peaked at 20% in the 12:00 UTC hour, the single yellow WATCH slot in the window, then decayed through the US cash session and held between 8% and 11% from 20:00 UTC onward as price discovery stayed orderly. Stress climbed from 74% to an 83% peak and settled near 80-81%, driven by crude and long-end yields rather than index path damage. Confidence held in an 87-89% band throughout.
outlookSummary: The forecast holds Tail in a 10-12% band through the remaining Asian overnight and the European session, where the governing mechanisms are headline discontinuity from the Strait of Hormuz and the European liquidity handover rather than trend persistence. Tail then steps up into the 12:30 UTC PPI, core PPI and claims block and peaks at 20%, mapping to WATCH, in the 13:00 UTC hour where post-release repricing overlaps the 13:30 UTC US cash open. It decays through the US afternoon past the 16:00 UTC EIA inventories and the 17:00 UTC 30-year auction, lifts one point into the power hour before the 20:00 UTC close, and returns to the overnight floor of 10% after the bell. The final slots edge back to 11-12% as sensitivity builds ahead of August CPI at 12:30 UTC on 11 September. Stress stays extreme throughout, peaking at 88% around the release, because the crude, rates and FOMC-pricing backdrop is a regime condition that persists independently of the observed index path.
